name: qr_read
description: Read QR symbols from pictures and say what was looked for when none is read: one row per input, decoded (version, level, mask, errors corrected, the payload's length and the file it was written to) or "not a symbol". It is written in the standard library alone: a PNG is read by a reader of its own (8 and 16-bit grey, RGB, palette and alpha, 1 to 4-bit grey and palette; not interlaced; a 16-bit sample is brought to 8 bits by the picture's own largest sample, and picture_notes says so), and a JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP or TIFF picture, an interlaced PNG and an animated one only where Pillow imports, Pillow being given these formats alone (an icon or any other format is not read; picture_reader says which reader read it). Pillow never runs in the tool's own process: a child is forked for each picture, sends its frames one after the other (it seeks to the next and never asks how many there are) and is killed (SIGKILL) when the tool's clock runs out, with its address space bounded on Linux (1 GiB more than it was forked with) and its CPU time by the clock; a JPEG of more than 256 scans (start-of-scan markers; a picture has one, a progressive one about ten) is refused before it is handed over. Every frame or page of a picture (an animated GIF, PNG or WebP, a TIFF of several pages) is searched, at most 64: the row names the frame that decoded (frame), the frames with the same payload, and any other frame's symbol with its own payload file (other_frames_decoded, however many different payloads the frames hold); frames is how many the picture has, and when the search stopped before the last was known (the clock, a frame Pillow does not read, the bound of 64, past which frames are neither counted nor searched) frames_at_least says how many are known instead, frames_not_read names what was not reached and the answer is partial. A PNG the built-in reader finds cut or corrupt is not passed off as whole: when Pillow reads it all the same (it fills what is missing), picture_damaged says so and the answer is partial. Nor is a JPEG cut short and given its end marker back (what a carver makes of a fragmented file; libjpeg fills the missing blocks with grey and Pillow says nothing): a JPEG Pillow decoded is walked by the tool itself, block by block through its Huffman codes (sequential or progressive, ISO/IEC 10918-1 Annexes F and G, no pixel decoded), its restart markers checked in order, and it must code every block its frame's size implies before its data ends, every component in a scan and, progressive, every coefficient to its last bit; one that does not is picture_damaged and partial. The walk takes at most 30 seconds and half of what the clock has left; a JPEG it does not take (arithmetic, lossless or hierarchical coding, a DNL height, a second frame header, a walk past its share of the clock) and the frames past the first of a multi-picture JPEG are named in jpeg_data_not_walked / jpeg_frames_not_walked and the answer is partial. Every symbol of a frame is read: a symbol read is masked out (its modules and half a module round them set light) and the frame searched again, then in the other polarity with every symbol read masked, up to 8 symbols a frame; the row's first symbol is the reading, the others are listed in other_symbols_decoded (frame, symbol, polarity, region_pixels, each with its own payload file), region_pixels is where each was read, and a frame with more than 8 (symbols_past_the_bound) or with finder patterns outside every symbol read that no reading made a symbol of (finder_patterns_not_read: another symbol may be there that these methods do not read) makes the answer partial. The status is derived from one list of what was not read or not judged (not_read_or_judged, every counter printed, zeros included): any counter above zero makes the answer partial, and partial_reasons are its sentences. RULES (they are in every answer and in every refusal too): (1) A decoded payload is a reading of a picture: it says what the symbol encodes, not who made it, when, or that a link in it was opened. Cite the picture, the payload file and version, level and mask; errors_corrected says how much of the symbol was repaired. (2) The payload is in a file, never in the answer: it can be a credential (an otpauth secret, a Wi-Fi passphrase, a login link). When payload_shape says so, or the case suggests it, run the job with secret_output: true and cite the file, not the text. (3) A symbol with a finder erased or overdrawn is read by mode repaint (auto tries it too): the grid is taken from the two finders left or from the box of the dark pixels, the fixed patterns are taken as the standard's, and the format word and Reed-Solomon decide. Pieces of one symbol go to mode fragments together, as images: [..], never one call a piece. (4) "not a symbol" is a statement about these methods on this picture (looked_for lists them) and holds only because the planted control was read first: a symbol under perspective, torn along a ragged line, of version 11 or above, or of another kind (Data Matrix, Aztec, a bar code) is not read here, and that is not its absence. WHAT IT DOES: the picture is thresholded (Otsu; dark on light, then light on dark); finder patterns are found by their 1:1:3:1:1 runs along rows and columns; the module grid is sampled through three finders and, from version 2, the alignment pattern (its centre taken as the middle of the places that match it best and then of its dark centre module, so that a clean symbol reads with no correction); the format word is read in both copies against all 32 valid words (BCH 15,5, up to three wrong bits); the mask is lifted; the codewords are corrected with Reed-Solomon; numeric, alphanumeric and byte segments are read (a kanji segment is written as Shift JIS pairs; an ECI designator, FNC1 and structured append are noted; of a structured append its position, never its parity byte, a digest of the whole message). Versions 1 to 10 (21 to 57 modules), levels L M Q H, masks 0 to 7. MODES: auto (default) tries the three-finder reading and then the repaint reading; finders only the first; repaint takes the grid from the two finders that are left (as neighbouring or as opposite corners of a square grid) or from the box of the dark pixels (box gives it, version fixes the size; box goes with mode auto or repaint, it is refused with finders and fragments, and with it only the box is read and looked_for says so), takes every fixed module as the standard's instead of reading it, lets the format word and Reed-Solomon decide (as a last resort, when neither format copy is within three bits of a format word, each of the 32 format words is tried and Reed-Solomon decides, a reading that needs more than a quarter of the check codewords being refused and, of those that decode, the strongest level taken: a codeword of a stronger level is also one of a weaker level whose blocks have the same lengths, which would decode with the wrong split of data and check codewords), and writes a repainted copy of the symbol (repainted_file, mode 0600); a box that reaches past the picture is refused for that picture; fragments takes several pictures that are rectangular pieces of one symbol at one scale: each is cut into modules at the module size its runs give, every place of every piece in the grids of the versions the pieces could fill is ranked on the fixed modules it would cover, and whole placements are scored on the format word and on how many Reed-Solomon blocks have zero syndromes, the first that decodes being the answer (placements names where each piece went). Each placed piece is then held against the symbol read (its corrected codewords placed again): a piece of another symbol of the same version and mask agrees on the fixed modules and is outvoted by Reed-Solomon in the data, so a piece that contradicts the symbol in any module is named in pieces_contradicting_the_symbol (with modules_contradicting_the_decoded_symbol in its placement: it is damaged there, or not a piece of this symbol) and the answer is partial. CONTROL: before any picture is read, a symbol made in the tool (version 3, level Q, random payload, three modules flipped) is read back by the same code, whole, with a finder erased (auto, repaint) and cut into four pieces (fragments), whose placements must contradict the symbol read in exactly the flipped modules; a failed control ends the call as failed without reading a picture, and self_test: true runs every control alone. So "not a symbol" means: this picture was read whole, these methods (looked_for lists them, with the counts of finder candidates, grids sampled, format words read and Reed-Solomon attempts) read no symbol from it, and the same code read the control. It does NOT read (not_read in every answer): versions 11 to 40, Micro QR, rMQR and other symbologies; a symbol under strong perspective or on a curved surface; pieces turned against each other, of different scale or not rectangular; a piece set with a hole beyond what Reed-Solomon corrects (missing modules count as light: no erasure decoding); frames past the 64th of a picture, and, by the built-in reader, an animated PNG's frames other than its default image; a picture of a format other than PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP and TIFF. THE PAYLOAD IS NOT IN THE ANSWER: it is written to qr-NN.payload.bin (mode 0600) in a new directory under $OUT (outside a job, under work/<agent>/tool-output), and the answer carries its length, its segments' modes and payload_shape (text, a URI, an otpauth URI, a Wi-Fi configuration, bytes that are not UTF-8: a kind read from the first characters, never the content); payload_holds_a_secret_shape is true for the two kinds that carry a credential. This tool does not declare secret output: an agent that expects a credential runs the job with secret_output: true. The picture's sha256 is printed; no digest of a payload is. Status: complete when every picture given was read whole, every frame of it searched, and judged; partial when a picture could not be read as a picture, was damaged, was a JPEG whose coded data was not walked, had frames that were not searched, had a frame past the symbol bound or finder patterns no reading explains, the clock (max_seconds) ran out, the placement search stopped at a bound, a placed piece contradicts the symbol read, or a payload could not be written, with partial_reasons; failed when nothing was judged (no picture decoded or found to hold no symbol: a piece set whose search was stopped is failed, not a negative). Bounds: at most 64 pictures a call, 256 MiB, 36,000,000 pixels and 100,000 rows a picture (the built-in PNG reader takes rows of up to 256 MiB inflated, and reads the clock every 1024 chunks and every 65,536 bytes of a row; the finder search walks a row's runs five at a time, never holding a list of them), 16 pieces, 4,000 whole placements scored and 20,000 steps of the placement search (each step reads the clock; a search stopped at either bound or by the clock is answered not finished, never not a symbol), 64 frames a picture. Measured with Python 3.12 on an Apple M-series host: the controls of the default call 0.02 s (a whole self_test, interpreter start included, under 0.1 s); a 145 x 145 pixel version 1 symbol 0.02 s; a 1920 x 1080 picture of flat blocks (no symbol) 0.07 to 0.1 s; a picture of random noise, the worst case (it is full of chance finder shapes), 1.4 to 2.5 s at 600 x 600 and 23 to 46 s at 2000 x 2000 (the spread is the same host under the load of other work), both polarities and the built-in reader's decode included; a job VM may be several times slower, and the clock then ends the call as partial; 16 pieces that place nowhere end at the bound of steps in about a minute there. Paths are printed as given. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer, status failed and interrupted, exit 128 + the signal, and a file that was begun is removed. Known limits of the claim: the encoder of the control and the decoder share one author's tables (they are checked against the count of data modules of each version and, in the tests, against two independent generators: one for versions 1 to 4 at level L, one for versions 1 to 10 at every level); a payload that decodes is a reading of the picture, and errors_corrected says how much of it was repaired.

image.description: One picture to read (a path; a PNG, or another format where Pillow imports)

images.description: Several pictures: each is read on its own (one row each), or, with mode fragments, all are pieces of ONE symbol and are placed together (at least two, at most 16)

mode.description: auto (default: three finders, then repaint), finders, repaint (a finder erased or overdrawn; writes a repainted copy) or fragments (images are pieces of one symbol)

box.description: [left, top, right, bottom] in pixels: the symbol's own extent without its quiet zone, for one picture in which other dark content defeats the box of the dark pixels (repaint reading only)

version.description: The symbol's version, 1 to 10, when it is known: only that size is tried (box and fragments)

module_pixels.description: fragments: the size of one module in pixels, when the pieces' own runs do not give it (1 to 512)

reader.description: auto (default: the built-in PNG reader, Pillow for the rest) or builtin (never Pillow)

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 90, 5 to 100; the manifest's timeout is 120). When it runs out the answer is partial and names the picture it stopped in

self_test.description: true: run only the planted controls and answer whether each passed. No evidence is read
